instructions: For the Mortar and Pestle Pesto
Add the garlic, salt, and nuts of choice to the mortar. Using the pestle, muddle the ingredients in a circular motion until it becomes a paste. - 1 clove garlic - 1 oz pine nuts

Add the herbs and/or greens to the mortar. Using the pestle, pound the leaves into the garlic paste. If the leaves are taking a while to break down, add a splash of olive oil. - 2 cup (~1 1/2 oz) basil leaves packed (optionally blanched)
Once the greens have broken down, add the cheese and combine using the pestle. - 1 ½ oz parmesan reggiano grated

Add a small amount of oil at a time, pounding in between to combine the pesto, until the pesto reaches your desired consistency. If your pesto begins to break, add another sprinkling of grated cheese. - 2 ¾ oz 1/2 extra virgin olive oil - 1 ½ oz parmesan reggiano grated

Use immediately or store the pesto in an airtight container. Before closing the lid, add a thin layer of olive oil on top of the pesto to prevent discoloring. Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
Combine the garlic, salt, and nuts of choice in the bowl of a food processor. Pulse the ingredients until they are the consistency of sand. - 1 clove garlic - 1 oz roasted almonds

Add the herbs/greens and cheese to the food processor and process until the ingredients are combined. - 1 ½ oz curly kale blanched - ½ oz parsley leaves - ¾ oz parmesan cheese grated - ¾ oz pecorino cheese grated
With the food processor running, slowly pour the olive oil down the feed spout. Continue processing until the sauce is thoroughly combined and homogenous. - 2 ¾ oz 1/2 extra virgin olive oil

Use immediately or store the pesto in an airtight container. Before closing the lid, add a thin layer of olive oil on top of the pesto to prevent discoloring. Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
